day_shape: 72 items: Trump weighs next move on Iran after Democrats seize Congress blaming the Iran war, two State Dept sanctions tranches (MANPADS network; shadow-fleet flags), fresh Strait of Hormuz tanker fires, IDF strike in south Lebanon, White House renews Iran national emergency.

threads.label: US midterm fallout and Iran war debate
threads.summary: Democrats took both chambers of Congress with the Iran war cited as a driver, and Vice President JD Vance publicly blamed the Israel relationship and Iran war for Republican losses. Reports said Trump is weighing renewed strikes or a negotiated settlement, while Senator Ted Lieu said legislation would be pushed to prevent war with Iran.

threads.label: US sanctions and Iran national emergency
threads.summary: The State Department announced two same-day actions: designations against a Belarus/Russia/Nigeria MANPADS procurement network, and measures against fraudulent ship-registry providers and a Türkiye-based aviation firm servicing sanctioned Iranian airlines. The White House published a continuation of the national emergency with respect to Iran in the Federal Register.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents
threads.summary: Defa Press said another tanker caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz after striking a sea mine, and reported UKMTO logging two projectiles striking a tanker 50 nautical miles north of Qatar's al-Shamal. The IRGC said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents, and South Korea plans to reposition its Cheonghae anti-piracy unit closer to the Strait.

threads.label: Iran nuclear and war-posture debate
threads.summary: Reports said growing numbers of Iranian clerics and officials are pressing leaders to reverse the pledge not to pursue nuclear weapons, with Tehran's debate turning to wider strikes and nuclear threats. Khamenei's office posted messages on 'absolute deterrence' and 'Iran ever stronger', while Iran International reported state TV aired a mock hanging of Trump.

threads.label: IDF operations in Lebanon and Gaza
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed Jamal Abu Saeed, Hamas military intelligence operations chief who held hostage Omer Shem Tov, in a Gaza City strike, and struck two suspects observing troops in Qabrikha, south Lebanon — Lebanon's health ministry reported one Amal-linked paramedic killed. Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir said the military would not allow Hezbollah to re-establish infrastructure in southern Lebanon.

threads.label: Iran-Russia military and transit links
threads.summary: Iran International, citing the Financial Times, reported Russia agreed to supply Iran with 90 helicopter-mounted precision missile launchers of the type used in Ukraine. IRIB said Iran and Russia signed a document transferring remaining Rasht–Astara railway land to the Russian side to advance field studies.

threads.label: Yemen file at UN and regional diplomacy
threads.summary: The Security Council met for a briefing on the 2140 Yemen sanctions committee ahead of 14 November, while IRIB and Defa Press carried Iranian denials of Kaja Kallas's remarks on Iranian interference and Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree's rejection of Saudi claims about a Medina missile interception. The Jerusalem Post reported Saudi Arabia and Syria signed military and financial agreements.
